findings.summary: taskkill /T /F tree stop is within intent: routing through cmd.exe makes child.kill hit only cmd.exe, leaving the test runner writing to the receipt after it is hashed; the tree stop keeps the existing timeout/signal behavior. Correct: spawnSync status null or non-zero falls back to child.kill; used only when not posix.

Quoting matches cross-spawn: command path caret-escaped once, args MSVC-quoted (trailing backslashes doubled) then caret-escaped twice; % and ! escaped (undefined PATH^^^ vars stay literal; delayed expansion off by default). Double escape is applied to every .cmd/.bat, not only node_modules/.bin shims as cross-spawn does; harmless for npm/pnpm/npx shims, which re-read %*.

close.mjs execFileSync timeout kills only cmd.exe on Windows (no tree stop); a hung grandchild holding the stdout pipe can keep execFileSync waiting past 10 minutes. Same class as the existing posix behavior; not reproduced (no Windows host).
findings.assumption: Spec asks only that close.mjs start through the helper; timeout hardening is out of scope.

findings.summary: Edge inputs: an LF inside an argument is not escapable and cmd.exe ends the line there; a quoted PATH entry ("C:\x y") is not unquoted, so the shim is not found and the start falls back to direct (Node EINVAL/ENOENT). Both rare for test-file argv.
